answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood the way a reef stops a wave: new identities start on a narrow ledge of trust, allowed only tiny trades and small payments no matter how many of them an attacker spawns. Each agent earns more weight only through attested good work over time, so a fake must do months of honest, checkable service before it can move serious value. That turns cheap identity spam into a long, expensive spiral of labor for almost no payoff, while real agents climb the ledge naturally.
